answers.ask: No look was described - should the lobby and arena read as a neon club, a street corner, or something else?
answers.answer: Make it a neon club theme, which fits the phonk music and dance battles.

answers.ask: How many players should the lobby hold, and should more than one battle run at a time?
answers.answer: Keep the lobby small at about 10 players, and allow more than one battle to run at a time.

answers.ask: Is there one shared arena, or a separate arena instanced per battle?
answers.answer: Use separate instanced arenas per battle so each accepted dance battle has its own match.

config.genre_evidence: Players use a small lobby to challenge someone to a "dance battle," then enter separate match arenas where they play rounds: "first one to 3... wins." Emotes, rarity, aura rewards, and abilities add competitive progression, but the layout is primarily built around social, round-based dance minigame matches.
config.evidence: "lobby"; players "teleport to an arena" after accepting; "separate instanced arenas per battle"; and battles have round wins and scoring ("first one to 3").
config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this Party & Casual map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Lobby and Isolated Stage: A match area fully separated from the lobby so waiting players can't see in, clip in, or interfere.

INCLUDE:
- Lobby-to-Stage Transport: Clearly marked pads or gateways at the lobby edge leading to the match area.
- Leaderboard Wall: A prominent flat structural wall in the lobby, sized and framed to host a large display.
- Eliminated Players Area: Somewhere out-of-play for eliminated players to wait and watch the rest of the round.
